brief.headline: Close the ₹82,500 annual price gap on measuring cups and push payment from 45 to 30 days to free up ₹10.19 L cash.

priceAsk.summary: Cut the measuring-cup price by 8.6% to match our best supplier.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.35/NOS (the price Premier Plastic gives us for the same item)
priceAsk.basis: We pay Mars ₹0.38/NOS for MESU. CUP 30MM TRANS.PP 2.5/5/10ML; Premier Plastic supplies it at ₹0.35/NOS — that 8.6% gap costs us ₹82,500 a year. The open market shows typical 28 mm caps at ₹0.85–0.95/pc, so our ₹0.38 ask is well inside the fair band and there's room to come down.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move payment from 45 days to 30 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹10.19 L cash freed up for us; another ₹5.10 L if we can push to 15 days more (to 15-day terms).

brief.financialLeverage: Mars Plastics publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. That means we build our ask around hard facts we do have: we pay 8.6% more than Premier Plastic for the same cup, the market shows our price is fair with headroom below, and we have five strong packaging alternates (including Manjushree, India's largest rigid converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue). With no published numbers to anchor on, push the price and payment asks firmly but frame the conversation as qualifying a second source for supply security — that keeps the door open and gives us the alternates we need.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹82,500 a year on one measuring-cup SKU alone.
Premier Plastic sells us the identical cup 8.6% cheaper.
Moving payment from 45 to 30 days frees up over ₹10 lakh cash for us.
The open market for similar 28 mm PP caps sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, so our ₹0.38 price is well inside the fair range.
Our annual spend with Mars is ₹1.24 Cr — meaningful volume to negotiate with.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (private, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — and already flagged as a top second-source candidate for packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (listed)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong, profitable and a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd (listed)
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging supplier with broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Mars publishes no financials, so we fly blind on their cash position and stability — watch for any supply hiccups and line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek fast if Mars wobbles.

Pushing hard on both price and payment at once may spook a private supplier with unknown finances — stage the asks (price first, then payment) or frame as a partnership to qualify a second source rather than a squeeze.
The ₹82,500 saving is real but small in absolute terms — don't burn the relationship over it; use it to anchor a broader review of all their SKUs and lock in the payment-term win.
We have strong listed and private alternates, but none are qualified or priced yet — start parallel RFQs with Manjushree and Mold-Tek now so we have leverage in 60 days.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to close the 8.6% price gap on the measuring cups — Premier gives us ₹0.35 and you're at ₹0.38 — and talk about moving payment to 30 days, which frees up over ₹10 lakh cash for us and helps both sides plan better.
